newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine firm shuts gold mine due to soft prices.
newsitem.headline: Philippine firm shuts gold mine due to soft prices.

text.p: Base Metal Mineral Resources Corp suspended operations of its gold mine in the southern Philippines after prices of gold tumbled to a 12-year low early this month, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
Base Metal, which is 40 percent owned by Philippine Gold Plc, closed its underground Masara gold mine in Davao del Norte province on July 7.
"We are reviewing our operations there to determine when is the proper time to resume operations," Base Metal's spokesman told Reuters.
Masara mine's ore mill was operating way below its 1,000-tonne capacity when it closed, he said.
Base Metal has 500 employees at the Masara mine.
The firm took over operations of the gold mine in 1994 through an agreement with Apex Mining Corp.
Gold prices plunged to a 12-year low to US$314 an ounce early this month.
Hong Kong gold closed at US$325.70/326.20 on Thursday.
